primitives.note: Q/W/E deal on-cast (or short-delay) magic damage on cooldown; R enemy-cast deals damage/CC but is irrelevant to a stationary-dummy damage fight, R self-cast is defensive-only

Q's missile passes through and can hit multiple targets, and shatters on hit to extend range/width; E's claw also hits enemies it passes through; against a single stationary dummy this collapses to a single hit unless the sim assumes multi-hit geometry
Glacial Path is cast then optionally recast (blink) 0.5s later; both casts count as separate ability activations for on-cast effects (e.g. Spellblade)
mana costs scale with rank and could matter for a low-mana build across a 15s fight, though base mana pool/regen aren't in this dossier
R's ice field can damage an enemy once every 4s while active (spreads/lingers for ~3s), functionally a single delayed tick rather than a true DOT in a 15s dummy fight
slows on Q/W/R do not affect damage or damage taken by a stationary dummy; included only for completeness, not needed for damage fight
R self-cast (stasis + missing-health heal) is purely defensive/survival-fight relevant, not used in the damage fight

Passive spawns an invulnerable/untargetable Frozen Thrall from an enemy champion death that deals a separate magic-damage explosion after 4s; cannot trigger in a dummy fight since the dummy target never dies, but is directly relevant to survival-fight setup if the attacking champion's kill triggers it

needsBespoke.why: All damage-relevant mechanics (plain casts, a multi-hit/pass-through projectile, a recast-blink ability, and a delayed-explosion pet triggered on enemy death) are expressible with existing primitives; the passive's death-trigger condition means it will almost never fire in a single-target damage fight (the dummy doesn't die) and can be treated as inapplicable there.

unsettled.question: In the single-dummy damage fight, does Ice Shard's pass-through/shatter mechanic ever produce more than one damage instance on the same target, or does the dummy's stationary single-body geometry mean it always hits exactly once per cast?
options: Always exactly one hit per cast against a single dummy
The shatter mechanic could hit the same dummy twice if the dummy occupies both the pre-shatter and post-shatter path (unlikely but sheet-ambiguous geometry)
quotes: deals {{as|magic damage}} to all enemies it passes through
If ''Ice Shard'' hits an enemy, it will shatter, increasing its width and maximum range.

unsettled.question: Should Glacial Path's recast (blink to the claw) be used at all in the max-damage rotation, given it deals no additional damage itself and its main function (repositioning) is explicitly out of scope (mobility ignored), but the recast does count as a second 'cast' for on-cast/on-cooldown-start interactions?
options: Skip the recast entirely since it has no direct damage and mobility is ignored, treat E as a single plain-cast
Always recast immediately since 'Starts on-cast' means cooldown timing is unaffected either way and recast could matter for item/rune on-cast triggers not modeled here
quotes: Both casts count as ability activations for the purposes of on-cast effects such as {{tip|Spellblade}}

unsettled.question: Is the P passive's Frozen Thrall explosion damage ever reachable in the damage fight (single stationary dummy that never dies), or should it be excluded entirely from the damage-fight simulation?
options: Exclude P entirely from the damage fight since the sole trigger (enemy champion death) cannot occur against a dummy that has health and never dies
Include P if the simulator's dummy is scripted to 'die' at some point (e.g. at the end of the 15s window) triggering a thrall spawn irrelevant to the timed kill/damage measurement
quotes: Whenever a nearby enemy champion dies, '''Lissandra''' spawns a ''Frozen Thrall'' from their corpse.

unsettled.question: For R's enemy-cast in the damage fight, does the ~4-second cooldown on the ice field's damage tick combined with the ability's 80-120s cooldown mean R is realistically cast at most once in a 15s fight, and should the field's chip damage plus initial CalculatedDamage both be counted as one combined instance per cast?
options: Count R as a single combined damage instance (CalculatedDamage + one ice-field tick) once per fight
Treat CalculatedDamage and the ice-field tick as two separate damage instances with distinct timings (spread delay of 1.5s)

spreads out from the target over {{fd|1.5}} seconds and covers the surrounding area for 3 seconds, dealing {{as|magic damage}} to enemies

proposal: Open with R (Frozen Tomb) enemy-cast on the dummy for its upfront magic damage plus the delayed ice-field tick, since its long cooldown means it should be used exactly once, as early as possible.
Follow immediately with Q (Ice Shard) on cooldown for its magic damage plus AP ratio; recast every time it comes off cooldown for the full 15s.
Weave in W (Ring of Frost) on cooldown between Q casts for its magic damage tick, since it has no cast time and low mana cost.

Cast E (Glacial Path) on cooldown for its damage; treat the ability as effectively resolved on the initial cast for damage purposes and either skip the recast or fire it immediately afterward if it interacts with on-cast item effects (see unsettled question), since the blink itself deals no damage and repositioning is irrelevant against a stationary dummy.

Repeat Q > W > E on cooldown for the remainder of the 15s window, prioritizing whichever ability is off cooldown to maximize total instances landed; basic attacks fill any remaining time between casts.
questions: Does the simulator model Lissandra's passive Frozen Thrall spawn at all, given the dummy never dies during the timed fight — should P be omitted from expected damage entirely?

Should R's enemy-cast be assumed castable on a stationary target-dummy without needing to path around cast-cancel conditions (untargetable/too-far/dies), i.e., does the dummy meet R's targeting requirements the whole fight?

In the 15s window, is there a fixed order expectation (e.g., always open with hardest-hitting ability R, or always lead with Q for cooldown-efficiency) that the simulator's ranking cares about, or does it evaluate all valid orderings and take the best kill time?

Does E's recast (blink) get executed in the simulated rotation at all, given the survival/damage fights have no walls or repositioning need, and does skipping it forgo any measurable damage or on-hit trigger opportunity?
